question.worked_solution:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

- Start with the graph of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$

- Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $4.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255908/assets/52177b289595a66bb5846d469c070db74371690fc3e321517c6e7c7658794da3.png)

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is ${y}_{max}=4$ and the minimum value is ${y}_{min}=-4.$ Therefore, the amplitude is:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude } & =\frac{{y}_{max}-{y}_{min}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4-(-4)}{2} \\  & =\frac{4+4}{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{2} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
